public_rationale: Altman's 2016 description concerned a board with representatives elected by broad parts of the world [e1]. The March 2024 corporate board announcement, September 2024 safety committee disclosure and October 2025 Foundation announcement do not establish that such a representative board materialized [e2, e3, e4]. These records are consistent with the historical premise, but do not prove that no qualifying board existed [e1, e2, e3, e4]. They therefore leave the conditional forecast unresolved: they establish neither a qualifying board's initial powers nor whether a government mandate required those powers [e2, e3, e4].
limitations: The available records do not conclusively establish nonexistence through October 28, 2026.
No founding documents establish a qualifying board's constituency, selection process, powers or applicable government requirements.
The forecast has no deadline; continued nonappearance cannot establish success.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The governance board Altman spoke of to The New Yorker in 2016 never materialized, and Marcus bets that if one does, it won't have any teeth unless a government mandate requires it to.
conditions: unless there is a government mandate that it have teeth

statement.excerpt: No such governance board ever materialized; if it does, you can bet it won’t have any teeth, unless there is a government mandate that it does.
statement.document_title: Scoop: What former employees of OpenAI are worried about

from_speaker: No such governance board ever materialized
unless there is a government mandate that it does
our_interpretation: The referenced board is the broadly representative external governance body Altman described in 2016, with representatives elected by wide parts of the world.
An ordinary corporate board or a committee of its directors does not by itself satisfy that description.
'Teeth' means binding authority to block, delay, or change consequential company decisions.
The forecast applies if that kind of board materializes without a government mandate requiring meaningful powers.
The historical premise is considered separately in the rationale, but does not turn an untriggered conditional forecast into a successful prediction.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying board is established without a mandate requiring meaningful powers, and its governing instruments show that its role is advisory and lacks binding authority at establishment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying board is established and obtains binding authority without a government mandate requiring that authority.

evidence.explanation: The original interview identifies an elected representative body. It prevents treating every later corporate oversight committee as the board contemplated by this claim.

evidence.explanation: The announcement describes substantive committee oversight, including authority to delay releases elsewhere in the same disclosure. This matters against a broad claim that company governance can never have powers, but it does not establish the representative external board that triggers this forecast.
The restructuring announcement describes nonprofit control of the business. It does not establish a board elected by broad parts of the world or resolve the forecast's government-mandate exception.
